tagline.text: A fishing town at the north end of Bantayan Island with Spanish fort ruins and a dried-fish market

location.label: Location
location.text: Northern Bantayan Island, Cebu Province, around Madridejos town

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half a day to one day

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000–3,000 (per person, one day staying in Santa Fe)

children.text: Madridejos is a fishing town at the northern end of Bantayan Island, known for Kota Park with its Spanish-era fort ruins, for sunsets and for its dried-fish market. Unlike beach-resort Santa Fe in the south, it shows simple island life.

Madridejos is a municipality at the northern end of Bantayan Island, with the Visayan Sea wrapping around its north and west and Daanbantayan to the east and Bantayan town to the south. It covers about 24 km², and as of 2024 has about 43,000 residents in 14 barangays. The largest barangay is Mancilang (about 4,900 people). It became its own town on January 2, 1917, separated from Lawis, and is said to be named for Benito Romero de Madridejos, then Archbishop of Cebu.

In the Spanish period a fort and a chapel were built here in Lawis. The chapel was dedicated to Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception and became a parish in 1928. During World War II, Japanese forces occupied the area in 1942 and Philippine Commonwealth troops liberated it in 1945. Because of this history, fort ruins and a lighthouse still stand along the coast.

The main livelihoods are fishing, poultry raising and tourism. Wikipedia says the town is called the "Little Alaska of the Philippines" for its rich fishing grounds, and that it once had the country's first canning factory, which was destroyed by bombing in World War II. Drying and processing fish and fishing remain at the center of the town's economy, so people come to buy danggit (dried fish) and dried squid.

As a destination, Madridejos is plain. With no glamorous resorts or busy streets, the focus is the fort ruins, the sea and the villagers, so the usual plan is to ride a motorbike here from Santa Fe for the day and watch the sunset at Kota Park. It is better thought of as the northern end point of an island loop than a place to stay long. One thing to know is that the north of the island is much quieter than the south. Unlike Santa Fe, where beach lodgings and restaurants are concentrated, Madridejos has few facilities for tourists, so bring water, snacks and cash in advance.

This is a seaside park on the Madridejos coast with the ruins of a Spanish-era fort (the Kota ruins). Entry is generally free, and a walkway, a beach, and a small pier and viewing platform facing the sea are said to make it a good place for sunset. One travel account says it is not worth a special trip unless you like fortifications, so expect the sea view rather than the ruins themselves. Accounts say the beach is busy at sunset with local families, so expect the feel of a neighborhood waterfront rather than a tourist spot. It is better for walking and looking at the sandbar than for swimming.

At Kota Point the Madridejos light station stands about 50 m inland from the shoreline, with a beach and a walkway beside it. Nothing is known about whether you can go inside the lighthouse, so go expecting to see only the outside.

Because it is in the northwest of the island, you can watch the sun set straight into the sea. Arrive about an hour before sunset to get a spot on the pier and platform, and check your motorbike headlight since it is dark on the way back.

Shops selling danggit, dried squid and dried shrimp are scattered around town. Prices are low because this is where the product comes from, and many shops will vacuum-pack it. If you are buying gifts, check the packing date and how dry the fish is. Danggit is usually fried in oil, and squid is grilled as a snack.

The church (Immaculate Conception Parish) and plaza in the town center are busiest on the December 8 feast day. At other times they are quiet, letting you see local life up close. Look around quietly during Mass.

The Isda (fish) Festival, held on the December 8 feast of the Immaculate Conception, is a sea festival celebrating abundance in fishing. Around this time the town has also held events such as cycling races. The program changes every year, so check the latest announcements.

A baywalk good for strolling is described along the waterfront in town. The midday sun is strong, so walk in the morning or at dusk. Because fish drying is active here, you may come across people cleaning fish and laying it out to dry.

blocks.title: The north end of an island loop

children.text: It is about 30–45 minutes from Santa Fe by motorbike, and the road that continues past Bantayan town is flat with little traffic. On the way you can see rice fields, poultry farms and fishing villages in one day.

items.subtitle: The Kota Park sunset route

Ride north through Bantayan town to Madridejos. On the way you can stop at the Obo-ob mangroves or the Bantayan town market.
Look around the dried-fish stalls in the town market and have a snack that doubles as lunch.
Arrive at Kota Park and walk around the fort ruins, the lighthouse and the beach.
Watch the sunset and return to Santa Fe before dark. The ride back takes about
30–45 minutes
A round trip from Santa Fe adds up to 1.5–2 hours of travel. Work backward from sunset so that you reach Kota Park one hour before it.

items.title: A one-day island loop
items.subtitle: From the south to the northern tip

children.text: Leave Santa Fe and look around the church and market in Bantayan town.
Walk through the Obo-ob Mangrove Eco Park.
Go north to Madridejos for lunch and a look at the dried-fish shops.
See Kota Park and the lighthouse and walk along the coast.
Watch the sunset and return to Santa Fe.
A one-day loop involves a lot of travel, so each stop will be short. Put the sunset stop last.

items.title: By bus and ferry from Cebu City

3–4 hours

Wikipedia describes a ferry from Cebu City via Santa Fe to Hagnaya of about 75 minutes, and a route by Ceres bus from the North Terminal followed by a jeepney through Bantayan taking about one more hour. Either way, confirm the transport and fare from the island arrival point to Madridejos at Santa Fe or Bantayan town the day before.

There is no regular city bus on the island. Public transport centers on tricycles and multicabs, so travel times can be long.
Madridejos is best in the dry season,
December–May
, when sunsets are often clear and motorbike travel is easy. Around the patron saint's feast on
December 8
the town is busy with the Isda Festival, so catch it if your dates match. Sunset time ranges roughly between 17:30 and 18:20 by season, so check that day's time and arrive an hour before.
In the rainy season,
June–November

, frequent showers can hide the sunset, and in typhoon season ferries may be canceled. Bantayan Island is flat and low, so strong winds do great damage; check the weather forecast. During Holy Week (late March to mid-April) the whole island is crowded.

There are small lodgings in Madridejos itself, but traveler lodgings are mostly in Santa Fe, so the usual plan is to stay in Santa Fe and come for the day. If you stay overnight in Madridejos, it will be mainly small guesthouses, so book ahead and check local conditions.

The food centers on dried fish and seafood. The most island-like meal is a breakfast of fried danggit or dried squid with garlic rice and egg, dipped in spicy vinegar. For a snack, puto balanghoy, a steamed cassava cake, sells for about ₱10. Village restaurants are generally cheaper than in Cebu City.

Around Madridejos there are not many places to eat late. The easiest choice is to return to Santa Fe after the sunset and have dinner at a beach barbecue restaurant. Restaurants near the market serve fried fish and soups at modest prices, so have lunch in town.
Arrive about an hour before sunset, and check your motorbike headlight and helmet because it is dark on the way back.
Prices of dried fish differ by shop, so compare two or three and ask for vacuum packing.
ATMs are few on the island and concentrated in Bantayan town. Carry cash in advance.
Kota Park is a fort ruin with stairs and low walls. Keep an eye on children so they do not climb.
The church and plaza are spaces for local worshippers, so ask permission before taking photos.
During the December 8 festival roads get congested and lodging runs short, so move early.
The Madridejos town market is liveliest in the morning. To see dried fish and fresh fish, arrive before noon.
The September 30, 2025 northern Cebu earthquake damaged some buildings on Bantayan Island. Check locally whether the church and public facilities are open.
Madridejos is a town with little published information. It is safer to check Kota Park's hours and facilities before you go.
When riding around the island by motorbike, return to your lodging before sunset because night roads are dark.
In the hot season there is little shade and the midday sun is strong. Bring a hat and water.
In typhoon season the whole island is prone to wind damage. Check the weather forecast before you travel.
Dried fish is sensitive to moisture and smell. If you pack it for a flight, seal it and check the carrying rules.
The beach near Kota Park is a neighborhood waterfront used by locals. Keep the noise down and take your trash with you.

The island's main town has an old coral-stone church, a market and the Obo-ob mangroves. It lies to the south of Madridejos.
Malapascua Island
, famous for diving, lies across the sea to the east of the island.
